Re: Senior Signal Processing Engineer

The 16-element adaptive array I brought to prototype at Sumuvire Wireless in 2018 was the first fully digital beamforming product the company shipped. That project is probably the best short summary of what I bring.

As Head of DSP at Sumuvire from 2011 to 2013, I directed the beamforming development group through the KW-100 architecture definition, establishing the signal chain design and the embedded test framework that the team still uses. The redundancy round at the end of 2013 put a stop to that, and the year that followed -- requalifying, trying to fill gaps in my theoretical background -- was not a productive one on paper. Returning in 2015 with a sharper sense of what I actually wanted from the work made the second stretch more focused.

On the software side, I wrote the production data pipeline for our antenna array calibration system in Python. About 8,000 lines handling measurement ingestion from the network analyser, automated gain and phase correction, and report generation. It replaced a collection of MATLAB scripts that an engineer had to babysit manually, and brought calibration turnaround from about two working days down to under four hours. The pipeline runs nightly in a Jenkins job now and nobody has to think about it, which is the point. I would not call myself a software developer first, but I can write code that holds up in production and that other people can read.

The SAR demonstrator project (2019–2021) was the most technically demanding work I have done at Sumuvire. Sustained airborne platform constraints -- thermal budgets in an unpressurised Cessna rack at altitude, GPS/INS time-tagging at the microsecond level, and the kind of RF measurement discipline that comes from troubleshooting an X-band front end in a hangar at minus fifteen degrees in January. I owned range compression and motion compensation for the programme and handled the English-language technical reporting to the customer.

The Kaikuvaara posting fits well. The combination of phased-array development with real hardware integration is close to what I have spent a decade doing at Sumuvire, and the chance to work on systems with larger apertures and more demanding specifications is the draw. Oulu is home and I have no plan to leave. I hold Finnish citizenship and a valid security clearance. I can be available at fairly short notice if there is interest.

Sven Kowalski
